first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 directly address both metrics through field-reduction and streamlining—mechanisms that improved first-week activation and completion rates durably in the past. Memory_91 reinforces that in-product messaging compounds onboarding gains. Simplify_onboarding targets the root friction rather than short-term acquisition volume. While memory_73 shows promotional_pricing can acquire price-sensitive SMBs, it materially harmed retention—misaligned with the primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue. Referral_incentive works on established customers, but current problem is new-account activation. Enterprise_sales_assist is valuable but orthogonal to the 6% activation decline in the broader base. Verifying memory_31 and memory_86 will confirm whether field-reduction and onboarding shortening mechanisms are replicable under current conditions and whether there are interaction effects or context-specificity we should account for before committing to this experiment.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both mechanisms work: memory_31 drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention risk; memory_86 delivered +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. Current state shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—simplify_onboarding directly addresses both. The verified retention profile is positive (memory_86) to neutral (memory_31 on SMB). Competitor pricing pressure makes retention risk from promotional_pricing unacceptable; activation_messaging alone won't reverse the 4-6% declines; referral_incentive targets wrong segment; enterprise_sales_assist doesn't move the primary friction. Standard_experiment scale is appropriate: test on self-serve SMB cohort first to replicate memory_31/86 conditions, measure activation lift and time-to-value, monitor 30-day retention for downside before broader rollout. This preserves the uncertainty about whether improvements generalize under current competitive and engagement conditions while committing to the highest-probability lever for sustainable qualified revenue growth.
